scope: Casting to a macOS AirPlay Receiver with airplay2-cli: discovery, pairing, the diagnosis of the start failure, and the URL-controls fallback with scheduled controls (runs A-C). Observer answers are recorded separately from telemetry. Periodic 'notification keys=type,name,item' events are omitted from the run lines.

receiver.settings: AirPlay Receiver on; Allow AirPlay for: Anyone on the same network; no password (user)
receiver.advertised: AirPlay and RAOP on port 7000, acl=0, no pw, features 0x38174fde4a7fcfd5 (Apple TV: 0x3c177fde4a7fdfd5)

host: Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200); MSVC Release static, airplay2-cli built in the D62 worktree
source_scope: Uncommitted D62 working tree. Runs A and the first B attempt used the fallback with seek as {type, time}; the second B attempt and C added kind/messageID to seek; C also had a temporary /scrub switch, removed afterwards. clang-format was applied after the runs (formatting only). Runs D-F: run D used the seek without an item; runs E and F add item {uuid} (the committed form).

findings: The Mac rejects the remote-control SETUP with 500 after a successful pair-verify; the URL session alone plays.
Pairing and the base SETUP wait for an on-screen consent; unanswered, the Mac returns 400 after about 15 s.
setRate 0/1 pause and resume; status extrapolation matched the Mac's reported position (8.9 vs 8.892 s).
The natural end reports the final position (131.567 s) then stopped: media_end.

seek without an item (with and without kind/messageID), legacy /scrub and Start-Position-Seconds are accepted and ignored; seek with item {uuid} lands (runs E, F; Mac log 'Sender seek to time is ... for item', seekErr 0; user observed).
